children: Britain opened books on Tuesday for the scheduled sale of several billion pounds of new 30-year debt, just a week after the 30-year benchmark yield hit its highest since 1998 and drew initial orders of more than £58 billion ($78 billion).
Price guidance for the sale via syndication of the 5.375% 2056 gilt (GB30YT=RR) (GBT5R56=) remains at 0.75-1.0 basis points above the yield of the 4.25% 2055 gilt (GBT4Q55=).
Lead bookrunners for the transaction are Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Santander and UBS.
Britain is due to issue £251 billion of government debt this financial year, around 9% of which is planned to be of long-maturity conventional gilts, though full allocations have not been decided.
